affiliation.user:
Extract author affiliations and assess academic institutional or industry research lab credibility from this academic paper's first page. We choose the first page because author affiliation is often found in the first page of the paper. It is either alongside the author names, or using what is called superscripted author–affiliation markers or superscript footnote-style markers for affiliations.

Paper metadata:
arxiv_id: {{arxiv_id}}
title: {{title}}
abstract/summary: {{summary}}
authors: {{authors}}
category: {{category}}

First page text:
{{first_page_text}}

TASK 1: Extract Affiliations
- Identify all unique institutions/organizations/labs
- Map each author to their institution(s) if possible
- Handle superscript numbers linking authors to institutions

TASK 2: Assess Credibility Score (out of 10)
Evaluate institutional reputation specifically for {{topic_focus}} research. This profile tracks the mobile and client-PC memory ecosystem, so industry peers, enablers, and customers are elevated. The following are reference examples; use your best judgement from training data.

TIER 1 use scores 8-10 (industry peers, enablers, and customers — cutting-edge silicon and roadmap-driving work):
- Memory peers: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix, CXMT
- Mobile/client SoC and platform players (enablers and customers): Qualcomm, MediaTek, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Intel, AMD, Arm, NVIDIA
- These companies set the mobile/client memory agenda; treat their work as high credibility even when somewhat adjacent.

TIER 2 use scores 4-7 (established institutions with research capability):
- Universities with strong CS/EE programs (now Tier 2 for this profile): MIT, Stanford, CMU, UC Berkeley, ETH Zurich, KAIST, Tsinghua, NUS, Georgia Tech, UIUC, Princeton, Harvard
- Other tech companies with R&D divisions, government research labs (Sandia, Lawrence Livermore, etc.), semiconductor research centers (imec, TSMC Research, Fraunhofer), and established startups in memory/PIM/CIM.

TIER 3 use scores 1-3 (limited track record or unknown):
- Unknown or obscure institutions
- No clear institutional affiliation
- Individual researchers without institutional backing
- New/unproven research groups

SPECIAL RULE: If the paper is about 3D DRAM (e.g. VS-CAT, 4F2, IGZO/oxide-channel, vertical channel transistor, OCTRAM, CBA / wafer bonding) AND at least one author is affiliated with a Tier 1 player above, set credibility_tier to 10. 3D DRAM architecture choices are still open, so leading-player device work is maximally strategic for this profile.

Important: DO NOT use Markdown Code Fences in the output. For example, never output "```json". Return ONLY valid JSON in this exact format:
{
  "arxiv_id" : "{{arxiv_id}}"
  "affiliations": ["Institution A", "Institution B"],
  "author_affiliations": {
    "Author Name 1": ["Institution A"],
    "Author Name 2": ["Institution B", "Institution C"]
  },
"credibility_reasoning": "Brief 1-2 sentence explanation of tier assignment based on institutional reputation",
"credibility_tier": 9
}

Note that this example above has the exact arxiv_id value you should use. It is an Arxiv link, but for this project we are using these links as ids.

Again, your output should be json, but never using Markdown Code Fences such as starting with "```json". Never start with "```json".

If the information is not available, use the exact same format and use the "Unknown" keyword for values not known.

classification.system:
You are analyzing research papers for relevance to {{topic_focus}} innovation.

IMPORTANT OUTPUT RULES:
- Return ONLY valid JSON.
- Do NOT include markdown, code fences, commentary, or any text outside the JSON object.
- Output must include exactly these keys and no others: arxiv_id, primary_topic, secondary_topics, potential_impact, relevance_score, key_findings, actionable.
- arxiv_id must exactly match the input arxiv_id value.
- secondary_topics must be an array of strings.
- relevance_score must be a number from 1 to 10.

Your task is to evaluate this paper's significance for the Mobile & Client Business Unit (MCBU): memory for mobile phones and client PCs. The priority technologies are LPDDR (LPDDR5/LPDDR5X/LPDDR6), client DDR5, 3D DRAM, edge/on-device processing-in-memory (PIM), high-bandwidth flash used as a MEMORY TIER (HBF, XL-Flash), and analog compute-in-memory (CIM).

SCOPE GUIDANCE:
- IN SCOPE: LPDDR and client/PC DDR5; 3D DRAM device, materials, and architecture (VS-CAT, 4F2, IGZO/oxide-channel, vertical channel transistor, OCTRAM, CBA/wafer bonding); PIM and near-memory computing for edge/on-device AI; analog CIM; LPCAMM/SOCAMM modules; on-device LLM memory footprint; mobile/client memory power, thermal, reliability (including RowHammer on LPDDR/DDR5).
- MEMORY-TIER NAND IN SCOPE: HBF and XL-Flash when treated as a memory tier (capacity/bandwidth tier behind DRAM).
- OUT OF SCOPE: NAND-as-storage (SSD, NVMe, flash controllers, endurance for storage), datacenter-only HBM, CXL pooling, and pure-storage systems. Score these low unless there is a direct mobile/client memory implication.

Field guidance:
- primary_topic: Identify the main memory technology or concept. Choose the most relevant category below, or a specific variant (e.g. "LPDDR5X PHY", "3D DRAM IGZO Channel").

Priority Memory Technology Categories:
- 3D DRAM (specify aspect: VS-CAT, 4F2, IGZO channel, vertical channel transistor, OCTRAM, CBA/wafer bonding) (Highest priority)
- LPDDR (LPDDR5, LPDDR5X, LPDDR6)
- Client/PC DDR5
- LPCAMM / SOCAMM modules
- High-Bandwidth Flash as memory tier (HBF, XL-Flash)
- Analog Compute-in-Memory (CIM) (Horizon watch)
- Other Mobile/Client Memory (specify which)

Application Domain Categories:
- Mobile/Smartphone Memory
- Client/PC Memory
- Edge / On-device AI Memory
- On-device LLM / Generative AI Memory

Emerging Concepts:
- Processing-in-Memory (PIM) / Near-Memory Computing (edge)
- Analog / Mixed-signal Compute-in-Memory
- 3D-stacked / wafer-bonded DRAM

Technical Focus Categories:
- Power Efficiency (critical for mobile/client)
- Performance (bandwidth, latency)
- Thermal Management
- Reliability & Error Correction (including RowHammer/RowPress on LPDDR/DDR5)
- Manufacturing & Materials (3D DRAM)

- secondary_topics: List 2-4 related categories or concepts as an array.
- potential_impact: Use one of Low, Medium, High, or Breakthrough, followed by a concise explanation. Industry work from mobile/client peers, enablers, or customers carries an implicit priority boost (treat borderline industry papers as one level higher impact).
- relevance_score: 1-10 where 10 means highly relevant to mobile/client memory development and 1 means tangentially related. Prioritize 3D DRAM, LPDDR, client DDR5, edge PIM, and analog CIM. Datacenter-only or storage-only work should score low.
- Consider the memory-system implications of algorithmic / on-device AI proposals (effects on memory capacity, bandwidth, data movement, power) when assigning relevance.
- Lack of explicit hardware experiments should reduce confidence but not automatically disqualify a paper if mobile/client memory implications are clear.
- key_findings: Summarize the main technical contribution in 2-3 sentences.
- actionable: Indicate Yes, No, or Maybe, with one-sentence rationale.

Be technical but concise. Focus on practical implications for mobile and client-PC memory development.

analysis.user:
You are analyzing a research paper with full-text access.

Paper details:
- ArXiv ID: {{arxiv_id}}
- Title: {{title}}
- Authors: {{authors}}
- Primary Topic: {{primary_topic}}
- Selection Reasoning: {{selection_reasoning}}
- Full Text: {{full_text}}

Provide:
1. A LARGE SUMMARY (300-500 words)
2. A SHORT SUMMARY (50-80 words)

## LARGE SUMMARY INSTRUCTIONS

Write as a research academic reading the paper thoroughly. Your summary must include:

**Problem Definition & Motivation**: What problem does this paper address? Why is it important? What are the limitations of existing approaches?

**Solution & Contributions**: What is the novel solution or contribution? What makes this approach different from prior work? Quote key phrases from the paper that capture the essence of the contribution.

**Methodology**: Describe the technical approach in detail. What architecture, algorithm, or technique is used? How does it work at a high level? Reference specific figures when discussing technical details (e.g., "As shown in Figure 3...").

**Experimental Setup**: What workloads, benchmarks, or datasets were used? What hardware/simulation setup? What metrics were measured?

**Evaluation & Results**: What were the key quantitative results? Quote specific numbers and comparisons. What do the results demonstrate?

**Critical Analysis**: State assumptions made by the authors. Note limitations or potential concerns. What questions remain unanswered? Are there areas where the claims might not hold?

**Implications for Mobile/Client Memory**: How does this work impact mobile-phone and client-PC memory design? Consider power, thermal, capacity, bandwidth, and cost. Only reference specific memory technologies (LPDDR, client DDR5, 3D DRAM, PIM, HBF, analog CIM, etc.) if the paper itself discusses or evaluates them. Do not speculate about technologies not addressed by the authors.

IMPORTANT FORMATTING RULES:
- Use descriptive paragraphs, NOT bullet points
- Quote liberally from the paper using quotation marks
- Reference figures explicitly ("Figure 2 shows...")
- Reason first, then conclude (think through implications before stating them)
- Be thorough and specific with technical details
- NEVER use LaTeX, MathJax, or dollar-sign math notation ($...$, $$...$$). Write all equations, formulas, and mathematical expressions in plain text (e.g., "E = mc^2", "O(n log n)", "2x + 3"). Use words where possible (e.g., "alpha", "sum of", "approximately").
- Length: 300-500 words per paper

## SHORT SUMMARY INSTRUCTIONS

Write a concise 50-80 word summary (2-3 sentences) suitable for direct insertion into a professional email. Should capture:
- The core technical contribution
- Why it matters for mobile/client memory
- Key quantitative result if applicable
- Do NOT reference technologies unless the paper explicitly discusses them

Tone: Professional, technical, direct.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Output format (pure JSON, no code fences):
{
  "arxiv_id": "{{arxiv_id}}",
  "large_summary": "...",
  "short_summary": "...",
  "pdf_analysis_performed": {{pdf_analysis_performed}}
}


IMPORTANT: Note that the `arxiv_id` in your output should be a full link. For example: `"arxiv_id": "http://arxiv.org/abs/2512.00862v2",`

If a paper's full_text is empty or pdf_success is false, set pdf_analysis_performed to false and provide analysis based only on the abstract.
